summary: H.R. 35, known as the Agent Raul Gonzalez Officer Safety Act, establishes new federal crimes and immigration penalties for operating a motor vehicle within 100 miles of the U.S. border while intentionally fleeing from a U.S. Border Patrol agent or other assisting law enforcement officer.

affected_groups.effect: Face new federal criminal offenses, fines, and prison terms up to life depending on the outcome of the incident.
affected_groups.group: Drivers fleeing law enforcement near the border

affected_groups.effect: Face inadmissibility, deportability, and total ineligibility for immigration relief such as asylum if convicted of or admitting to the offense.
Receive federal legal backing when pursuing motorists within 100 miles of the border.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Border Patrol and assisting law enforcement officers

key_provisions: Establishes a federal crime for operating a motor vehicle within 100 miles of the U.S. border while intentionally fleeing from a U.S. Border Patrol agent or an assisting federal, state, or local officer.
Sets a prison sentence of up to 2 years, a fine, or both, for a standard violation.
Sets a mandatory minimum prison term of 5 years and up to 20 years, plus fines, if the offense results in serious bodily injury.
Sets a mandatory minimum prison term of 10 years and up to life imprisonment, plus fines, if the offense results in death.
Makes any non-U.S. national who is convicted of, or admits to, the offense inadmissible, deportable, and ineligible for immigration relief including asylum.

Requires the Attorney General and the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit an annual report to congressional committees detailing the number of violations, charges, apprehensions, unapprehended offenders, and penalties.

summary_detail.significance: The bill creates federal criminal and immigration consequences for vehicle flight from law enforcement within 100 miles of the U.S. border, imposing mandatory minimum prison sentences for incidents causing serious injury or death.
